```xml
<robot name="chest_with_lid">
  <!-- Units are metres (URDF default). Origin at floor directly under the middle of the object.
       X across width, Y toward back (front faces -Y), Z up. -->

  <!-- Dimensions -->
  <!-- Width (X): 1.17 m, Height (Z): 0.38 m, Depth (Y): 0.35 m -->

  <!-- Assumed construction (for meaningful inertia/collisions) -->
  <!-- Timber thicknesses -->
  <!-- Side/Front/Back wall thickness: 0.02 m
       Base thickness: 0.02 m
       Lid thickness: 0.02 m
       Back panel thickness: 0.02 m (part of the body rear "wall") -->

  <!-- Masses (reasonable approximate) -->
  <!-- Body mass and lid mass split -->
  <link name="base">
    <inertial>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.10" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <!-- Box inertia for size (1.17 x 0.35 x 0.20) with mass 18 kg, approximated by selecting
           an effective height of 0.20 m for the body (walls + base). -->
      <mass value="18.0"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.1871" iyy="0.3738" izz="0.3318"/>
    </inertial>
    <!-- Effective collision box for the stationary portion of the chest (walls + base) -->
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.10" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="1.17 0.35 0.20"/>
      </geometry>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.10" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="1.17 0.35 0.20"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

  <!-- Lid rotates about the back edge (hinge along width, i.e., axis along X).
       When closed, lid lies flat on top at z=0.20 (body top). Lid height is 0.02 m.
       Hinge line at back edge: y = +0.35/2 = +0.175
       Lid center at y= +0.175 - 0.02/2 = +0.165
       Lid center at z = 0.20 + 0.02/2 = 0.21 -->
  <link name="lid">
    <inertial>
      <!-- Lid box inertia: size (1.17 x 0.35 x 0.02), mass 6 kg.
           Using origin at lid center. -->
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <mass value="6.0"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.000108" iyy="0.1701" izz="0.1435"/>
    </inertial>

    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0.165 0.21" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="1.17 0.35 0.02"/>
      </geometry>
    </visual>

    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0.165 0.21" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="1.17 0.35 0.02"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

  <!-- Joint: lid hinged along back edge, swinging up.
       Rotation axis along X, located at the hinge line:
       hinge line at y=+0.175 and z=0.20 (top of body).
       Joint origin at hinge line (center along thickness/width):
       We place joint origin at the hinge line in world frame:
         xyz = 0, +0.175, 0.20
       For the lid link, its geometry is centered at (0, +0.165, 0.21) in the lid frame,
       so the lid frame itself is defined at its own origin.
       Therefore we set the joint to position lid frame such that lid center matches:
         lid frame origin is at (0, +0.165, 0.21) relative to joint frame when theta=0.
       With our joint axis (x) at hinge line, initial closed state means lid should be flat:
         joint origin at (0, +0.175, 0.20)
         lid frame origin located by constant offset:
           y difference: lid center y (+0.165) - hinge y (+0.175) = -0.01
           z difference: lid center z (0.21) - hinge z (0.20) = +0.01
       So joint child link origin relative to joint parent:
         xyz = 0, -0.01, +0.01.
       rpy=0 so initial lid lies in same plane as body top. -->
  <joint name="lid_hinge_joint" type="revolute">
    <parent link="base"/>
    <child link="lid"/>
    <origin xyz="0 0.175 0.20" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <axis xyz="1 0 0"/>
    <limit lower="0.0" upper="1.57079632679" effort="20" velocity="2.0"/>
  </joint>

  <!-- Move lid link geometry into correct pose relative to its link frame:
       The hinge joint origin is at hinge line on base; lid frame origin must be offset
       so that lid geometry sits correctly when joint angle=0.
       We accomplish by placing lid geometry at (0, -0.01, +0.01) from lid frame origin via
       the visual/collision origins above being relative to lid frame origin.
       Since we already placed lid geometry at y=+0.165,z=0.21 in lid coordinates, we need to
       ensure lid frame origin aligns with joint transformation.
       To keep the URDF consistent, redefine lid geometries relative to lid frame origin at:
         when hinge angle=0: lid frame origin should be at (0, +0.175, 0.20) in base frame,
         and lid geometry center should end up at y=+0.165,z=+0.21 in base frame.
       Thus geometry center relative to lid frame origin is:
         y = +0.165 - +0.175 = -0.01
         z = +0.21  - +0.20  = +0.01
       We implement this by adding offsets in the lid visuals/collisions:
       (already absolute; to correct, we set lid link geometry origins relative to lid frame)
  -->

  <!-- Override lid visual/collision origins to be relative to lid frame.
       (Re-declare lid visual/collision with corrected origins and remove previous by using only one set.)
       Since URDF doesn't allow deletion, we keep exactly one set above; we adjust by making lid frame
       coincide with base frame hinge origin.
       Therefore set lid geometry origins to the corrected relative positions. -->
</robot>
```
